federation_scope.downstream_owned_scope: AI-assisted development practice, workflow, governance, verification, evaluation, adoption, implementation, and operating-model implications.
federation_scope.upstream_owned_scope: Broad AI companies, products, models, developer tools, agentic frameworks, MCP servers, and general techniques.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub Copilot content exclusions reach app and CLI agentic workflows
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub says the Copilot app and Copilot CLI now respect enterprise, organization, and repository content-exclusion policies so excluded files are not used as context in agentic workflows.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Content-exclusion policies are becoming a reusable context-governance control for coding agents, not just editor autocomplete. Local practice should treat excluded paths as a first-class context boundary during source retrieval, agent execution, and audit review.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Record as a downstream governance lens for sensitive-source exclusion and context-selection policy.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub adds enterprise-managed default model settings for Copilot
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub says Copilot Business and Enterprise administrators can set the default model for new conversations through managed settings and optionally allow enterprise teams to override it through team mappings.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Model choice is moving into team-level operating policy. Local adoption guidance should separate default model governance, team exceptions, and user override rights from broad model benchmarking.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Capture as a managed-settings practice for team-specific assistant defaults and exception handling.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub previews Copilot code-review approval authority
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub says Copilot can now assess when a pull request is ready to approve, and administrators can authorize Copilot to sign off. The approval feature is off by default and configurable at enterprise, organization, and repository levels.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI review is crossing from advice into delegated review authority. Local review gates should distinguish AI-generated findings, AI readiness assessments, and any configured approval authority from human approval obligations.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route to intelligent code review and lifecycle AI review gates as a practice-level authority boundary.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub exposes temporary user-budget expiration for Copilot
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub says Copilot Business and Enterprise administrators can set optional expiration dates for individual user budgets, including expiration at the next billing cycle or a specific date.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Temporary budget overrides are now governable lifecycle artifacts. Adoption practice can pair pilot access, incident response, onboarding bursts, or role changes with automatic spending cleanup.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Record as an operating-model pattern for time-boxed assistant spend and pilot governance.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub CLI supports attaching media to issues and pull requests
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub says gh v2.99.0 adds a repeatable --attach flag for issue and pull-request commands, supporting images and videos with Markdown references and alt text.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agents can attach screenshots or videos directly when filing bugs, creating PRs, or reporting verification evidence. This strengthens source-ingest and review workflows where visual proof matters.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route to source-workflow and verification evidence patterns, especially frontend and UI regression repair.

qualifying_findings.title: GitHub adds Claude Fable 5.1 to Copilot with retention policy gates
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub says Claude Fable 5.1 is available in Copilot surfaces for long-horizon coding and knowledge-work tasks. The policy is off by default for Copilot Business and Enterprise administrators, requires data retention by default, and has a time-bound zero-data-retention exemption for eligible enterprises.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Long-horizon agent model adoption now carries explicit retention and safety-classifier gates. Local practice should route model availability details upstream while preserving the downstream decision pattern: administrator enablement, retention review, and exception expiry.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Keep only the retention-gated model-enablement practice in this wiki; route model capability details upstream.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI expands Codex desktop workflows beyond code editing
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: OpenAI says Codex desktop can operate apps on a computer, use plugins, generate images, remember preferences, work across developer workflows such as PR review and multi-file or multi-terminal views, and take on ongoing repeatable work.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Coding-agent workflows are extending into desktop, browser, visual, plugin, memory, and recurring automation surfaces. Downstream coverage should focus on approval boundaries, progress visibility, multi-agent coordination, and local-workstation safety rather than broad Codex product coverage.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Use as evidence for supervised desktop-agent workflows, plugin governance, and recurring task operating rules.

qualifying_findings.title: Obot publishes practical tool-call audit trail schema
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Obot describes an AI agent audit trail schema for tool calls, including call ID, session, actor, tool, arguments, result status, authentication, policy decisions, request metadata, outcomes, and storage expectations.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Tool-call logs are being framed as governance evidence rather than chat history. Local MCP practice should preserve delegated authority, policy decision, and result-state evidence for troubleshooting, security review, and compliance.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route to tool-call governance and audit-log evidence patterns.

qualifying_findings.title: GAICC defines agentic AI governance around delegated authority
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GAICC frames agentic AI governance as controlling delegated authority, with inventory fields for agent identity, owner, purpose, model, tool scope, data classes, credentials, autonomy tier, oversight mode, review dates, and decommission triggers.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The article gives a concrete inventory shape for AI development agents and their tool bindings. Local governance pages can use it as public evidence for treating coding agents as first-class risk assets with lifecycle review.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Use as a downstream agent-inventory, autonomy-tier, and review-cadence practice source.

qualifying_findings.title: Oracle demonstrates governed MCP, A2A, A2UI, and MCP Apps boundaries
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Oracle describes a reference architecture where MCP exposes governed database operations, A2A connects host or agent communication, A2UI lets agents declare host-rendered interfaces, MCP Apps provide sandboxed UI resources, and the database retains transaction and audit authority.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a concrete application pattern for separating agent intent, tool execution, UI rendering, human approval, and authoritative transaction state. Local pages should capture the control-boundary pattern and route protocol or product background upstream.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route to agent application patterns for explicit execution authority, UI sandboxing, and approval handoff design.

qualifying_findings.title: Zop argues each AI assistant needs a separate grant and audit trail
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Zop argues that sharing one access token across multiple AI assistants prevents platforms from identifying which assistant performed a write, and says each assistant needs its own grant and traceable audit trail.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent identity should not collapse into a shared token. Local approval and MCP governance guidance can use this as evidence for per-assistant grants, revocation isolation, and write-action attribution.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route to agent identity, delegated authority, and audit trail practice.

qualifying_findings.title: Think Different recommends time-boxing AI coding agent loops
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Jakub Jirak argues that agent loops should be time-boxed and preceded by a short checklist covering acceptance criteria, test-suite fit, and rollback path. The article suggests tracking shipped-change stability and review round trips rather than accepted suggestion counts.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a direct practice update for planning loops and AI-assisted TDD: constrain delegated work by time, explicit success criteria, test relevance, rollback, and outcome metrics.
qualifying_findings.local_practice_implication: Route to orient-inspect-patch-verify loops and verification acceptance gates.
